mutants.description: The episode start is detected only in S_RUN: a first cause captured during soft start does not latch fault_time
mutants.reason: With ss_active high and run_active low, a first cause sets its fault_reg bit but fault_time stays 0, and stays 0 for the rest of the episode because fault_reg is no longer empty.

mutants.description: OVP inference is suppressed while an overcurrent window trip is live, on the assumption that the latch trip then belongs to the overcurrent
mutants.reason: An analog trip (latch_state high, latch_assert low) that coincides with window_trip or window_trip_SS while running sets only the OVERCURRENT bit; fault_reg[4] is never set.

mutants.description: Recording LATCH_ASSERT withdraws an already recorded OVP bit, treating the two latch origins as mutually exclusive in the record
mutants.reason: OVP captured first and latch_assert rising later in the same running episode leaves fault_reg with LATCH set and OVP cleared, although bits must only be cleared by a host read.

mutants.description: The record is judged empty from the four lower cause bits only; a recorded OVP does not count as an open episode
mutants.reason: In an episode whose only recorded cause is OVP, fault_time is re-latched on every clock a cause is live, so it follows timestamp_ms or jumps to the time of a later cause instead of holding the start time.

mutants.description: UVLO is recorded only as the first cause of an episode; a UVLO that follows another recorded cause is treated as a consequence and dropped
mutants.reason: With a cause already in fault_reg and the converter still running, uvlo_state going high no longer sets fault_reg[1].

mutants.description: LATCH_ASSERT is recorded only once the debounced SCR readback confirms it, not when the CPLD asserts the trip
mutants.reason: latch_assert high while latch_state is still low (the readback lags the trip) sets no LATCH bit; if running ends before latch_state rises, fault_reg[3] is never set, while fault_time is still latched for the episode.

mutants.description: fault_time is cleared by a host read only when the converter is stopped; a read during S_SS or S_RUN clears fault_reg but leaves the old start time
mutants.reason: After a read while running with no cause live, fault_reg reads 0 but fault_time keeps the previous episode's timestamp instead of returning to 0.

mutants.description: The three bytes of timestamp_ms are latched into fault_time in reversed order
mutants.reason: fault_time at the start of any episode differs from timestamp_ms whenever the top and bottom bytes of the timestamp are not equal.

mutants.description: fault_time is cleared when the converter stops, instead of being held until the host reads the record
mutants.reason: Once ss_active and run_active both drop after a fault, fault_time returns to 0 while fault_reg still holds the causes, so the start time is lost before the host can read it.

mutants.description: OVP is inferred from any disagreement between latch_state and latch_assert, not only from the latch set without the CPLD's trip
mutants.reason: While running, latch_assert high before the debounced latch_state reads back sets the OVP bit as well as LATCH, reporting a CPLD-originated trip as an analog overvoltage.
